defects: The finite-sublevel-sets hypothesis is spelled out as an explicit predicate (`∀ B, Set.Finite {x | h x ≤ B}`) rather than going through the `Northcott h` typeclass used in gold — content-equivalent assuming `Northcott` unfolds to exactly this predicate, but structurally an unbundled rather than typeclass-based formalization.

The growth witnesses n, b, c are packaged as an existential hypothesis (`∃ n, ∃ b c, ...`) rather than as universally-quantified implicit arguments as in gold — logically equivalent as an overall implication (since the conclusion doesn't mention n, b, c), but a different quantifier structure for the hypothesis itself.

The conclusion is stated as `Set.Finite {x : G | orderOf x ≠ 0}` instead of `Finite (torsion G)` — provably equivalent via standard facts (`orderOf x ≠ 0 ↔ IsOfFinOrder x`, and the torsion subgroup's carrier being `{x | IsOfFinOrder x}`, plus `Set.Finite ↔ Finite` on the coerced subtype), but does not directly use the named `torsion` subgroup from gold.
